summary: Tadeusz Pobożniak worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned an M.A. (~1931–1938) and Ph.D. (~1945–1948) at Jagiellonian University, studying under Helena Willman-Grabowska and Jan Michał Rozwadowski, and served there as professor (~1954–1975).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tadeusz Skorupski earned his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978. He served at SOAS University of London as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).

Tai-shing Wut specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998) and served as assistant professor at City University of Hong Kong (2009–2014).

Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Shuchiin University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held an attested post between 1994 and 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and Graduate Theological Union (Ph.D.), was adjunct professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994), and teaches at Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).

Taijun Inokuchi works in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and represented The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying under Tetsujiro Inoue and Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo, he earned his doctorate there in 1923 and became professor of Indian philosophy in 1912.
Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. from Ryukoku University in 2016. He also served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and completed a Ph.D. at Toyo University (1994), serving at Koyasan University as assistant professor (~1978–1993) and professor (~1993–2013; attested 2026).
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1933. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).
Taira Shidehara was a historian and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896), he held posts there (~1900–1919) and at Tokyo University of Education (~1903–1906).

Tairyo Makita worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1946; 1949–1976), Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~1982–1988), and president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997).
Tairyu Tsunoda specializes in Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studying under Kodo Sawaki (~1935–1965). He founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958) and earned a master's at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1964), later serving as professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2006).
Taishun Mibu was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University, graduating in 1937, and later served there as library director (~1958–1979).

Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo (M.A., Ph.D.), and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor at Smith College (1971–1998).
